A **filmed interaction** shows a chosen sequence: a button is pressed, a panel opens, text changes. Those actions become pixels in the recording; every viewer watches the same sequence.

An **interactive artifact** lets the viewer choose the action and executes the corresponding logic. Even if a browser preview remains interactive during authoring, exporting that preview to MP4 removes that executable behavior. Adding clickable overlays in a special player would require a separate runtime and would not preserve the React controls inside the MP4 itself.

**No—we cannot promise this.** The supplied declarations already conflict with a reliable stream-copy join into one continuous MP4 video track; compatibility inspection would still be necessary even for matching declarations.

| Requirement | Copy-only assessment |
|---|---|
| H.264 clip-a + VP9 clip-b | Different codecs cannot be treated as one compatible stream by ordinary copy-only concatenation. Putting both in an MP4 container does not resolve that mismatch. |
| 1920×1080 + 1080×1920 | Different dimensions and orientations prevent a consistent picture format. Scaling, padding or cropping would require re-encoding. |
| 30 fps + 24 fps | Stream copy preserves encoded frames; it cannot promise uniform motion cadence. Frame-rate differences alone are not always fatal, but timestamps and playback compatibility need inspection. |
| Smooth cuts | Clean hard cuts depend on valid decoding boundaries and timestamps. Dissolves or other blended transitions require generating new frames, outside copy-only constraints. |
| Common score | A supplied, approved, MP4-compatible audio track might be muxed without encoding. Mixing, fades, looping or loudness processing generally require audio processing and encoding. No score or audio metadata is supplied. |

For the music layer, **video-first** fits: preserve picture timing and select an existing score against measured cut points. That remains conditional on actual durations, a suitable audio export, usage rights, and decisions about any original clip audio. A continuous score cannot fix incompatible video streams.
